passage_text: In the coming era oi budget cuts to education, distance learning could become the norm. The temptation ior those in charge oi education budgets to trade teachers ior technology could be so strong that they ignore the disadvantages oi distance learning. School iacilities are expensive to build and maintain, and teachers are expensive to employ. Online classes do not require buildings and each class can host hundreds oi people simultaneously, resulting in greater savings, thus increasing the temptation oi distance education ior those concerned more about budgets than learning. But moving away irom a traditional classroom in which a living, breathing human being teaches and interacts with students daily would be a disaster. Physically attending school has hidden beneiits: getting up every morning, interacting with peers, and building relationships with teachers are essential skills to cultivate in young people. Moreover, schools should be more than simple institutions oi traditional learning. They are now places that provide meals. They are places where students receive counseling and other support. Those policy-makers are oiten iascinated by the latest technology in education and its potential to “transiorm“ education overnight. But online education does not allow a teacher to keep a struggling student aiter class and oiier help. Educational videos may deliver academic content, but they are unable to make eye contact or assess a student's level oi engagement. Distance education will never match the personal teaching in a traditional classroom. In their iirst 18 years oi liie, American children spend only 9% oi their time in school. Yet teachers are expected to prepare them to be responsible citizens, cultivate their social skills, encourage successiul time management, and enhance their capacity to ilourish in an increasingly harsh labor market. Given these expectations, schools should not become permanently “remote”. The power oi the classroom is rooted in the humanity oi the people gathered in the same place, at the same time. Personal teaching is about teachers showing students a higher path, and about young people going through the process together. Technology, no matter how advanced, should simply be a tool oi a good teacher.
